View SOFI Reports The department is committed to providing timely and accurate financial information to support informed decision-making and maintain the public’s trust in the District’s fiscal management. ## Financial Reports Audited Financial Statements Every year, the District of Houston prepares and submits its audited financial statements for the previous fiscal year to the Ministry of Community, Sports, and Cultural Services, as required under the Community Charter. The District also maintains its financial statements as permanent public records. The audited financial statements for the years 2011 through to the current year have been made available through this website. For previous years, please contact the Director of Finance. View Audited Financial Statements Statement of Financial Information Reports The District prepares a report annually in order to comply with the  Financial Information Act. Its primary purpose is to provide transparency about how public funds are raised, spent, and managed, allowing citizens and stakeholders to review financial operations.  The reports for the years 2013 through to the current year have been made available through this website. For previous years, please contact the Director of Finance.  View SOFI Reports Financial Plans The financial plan outlines the District’s projected revenues, expenditures, capital investments, and funding priorities over a five-year period. Adopted annually by Council, these plans help ensure the responsible management of public funds while supporting municipal services, infrastructure improvements, and long-term community goals. 1. Purpose The purpose of this policy is to ensure that compensation is fiscally responsible and fairly reflects the level of duties and responsibilities of the role of elected officials. 2. Scope This Policy applies to all City of Greenwood elected officials. 3. General The City of Greenwood Council members are paid remuneration and expenses in relation to the discharge of their duties as an elected official. 4. Interpretation The Interpretation Act applies to this policy. 5. Definitions In this policy "Council" has the same meaning as in the Council Procedure Bylaw; 6. Guiding principles 1. Remuneration a) Council members will be paid remuneration, as set out in Schedule “A”. b) The annual remuneration will be paid pursuant to the provisions and policies of the City's payroll system. 2. It manages financial reporting and control, oversees the implementation of financial management policies, and provides financial information and advice to council, District departments, and the general public. The following services are the functions of the Finance Department: * Day-to-day accounting * Accounts receivable and payable * Monthly reporting * Annual reporting to external agencies * Fiscal planning and community engagement related to the annual budget process * Financial analysis * Financial plan development * Cash flow forecasting * Management of DOI reserves * Tax collection * Utility Billing The Director of Finance is Council’s financial adviser and is expected to provide advice on financing capital projects, developing five-year plans (which include both operating and capital expenditures), the legality of expenditures, and taxation policy. In addition to the usual accounting functions and the preparation of applicable bylaws and policies as they relate to the municipality, the Director of Finance is responsible for the safekeeping of money and securities, investing funds and ensuring that local government expenditures are made in accordance with policy and the law.
